_meta.topic: Construction choices and costs for a life simulation: professionals, cost by specification, materials, site work, demolition, multi-unit and condo creation, delays and change orders, contracts and payment schedules, occupancy certificates
_meta.method: Web search plus direct reads of primary documents. Where a PDF was read in full (pdftotext), confirmed=true. Where a figure came only from a search-engine summary or a secondary site, confirmed=false and the note says so.

sourceTypeKey.government: statute, regulation, official fee schedule or government statistics
sourceTypeKey.professionalBody: trade association, chamber or professional institute
sourceTypeKey.costConsultant: quantity surveyor / cost consultancy publication (RLB, Altus)
sourceTypeKey.industrySurvey: industry survey by a publisher (Zonda Cost vs Value, KPMG, McKinsey)
sourceTypeKey.lawFirm: law-firm client alert summarizing a statute
sourceTypeKey.secondary: aggregator or contractor website; used only when no primary figure was found

_meta.currency: Figures in the currency of the jurisdiction: USD, CAD, MXN, GBP, EUR.
_meta.rule: Nulls where nothing is published. Nothing invented. Ranges from secondary sites are marked confirmed=false.

feeAsPercentOfConstruction.note: AIA publishes no fee schedule (antitrust). AIA B101-2017 leaves compensation blank for the parties to fill. Secondary sources commonly quote 8-15% of construction cost for full-service custom residential, 15-20% for renovations; that range is NOT an AIA figure.

billingMethodShare.value: Percentage-of-construction-cost method used for about 12% of billings in 2023; stipulated sum about 33% of billings on residential/institutional work
billingMethodShare.publisher: Archinect reporting AIA Firm Survey data

architectMedianPay.note: From search summary of the BLS page; wage, not a client billing rate.

feeScale.note: RIBA fee scales were mandatory for over a century, 'recommended' from 1982, 'indicative' from 1992 and abolished in 2009 after Office of Fair Trading pressure; the Competition Act 1998 bars published scales. RIBA now offers a resource-based Fee Calculator for Chartered Practices, RIBA Business Benchmarking (charge-out rates, salaries) and the 'Good Practice Guide: Fees' (2021).

RIAI can no longer publish recommended fee scales (competition law). It publishes an annual scatter of fees charged vs projected building cost by building type; for one-off houses, renovations and extensions the spread is roughly 4-16% of construction cost depending on size. Extensions up to about EUR 500,000 are commonly 9-11% plus VAT (practitioner source).
feeScale.publisher: Mark Stephens Architects (secondary, describing RIAI data)

typicalStageSplit.note: Practitioner-reported drawdown pattern, not an RIAI rule.

value.formula: H = CBM x V x FI x FGE x FM x FA x FR x FACP x FEPE
value.CBM_basis: Parametric cost for Vivienda Social type T11 (CMIC), November 2022; the arancel says it must be updated to the date of calculation
value.workedExample: 256 m2 two-level mid-range house remodel in Campeche, concept + anteproyecto only: H = MXN 28,334.16 (Nov 2022)
value.impliedFullFee: About 4.0% of the parametric construction value (CBM x V x factors) for a complete executive project
value.uptake: FCARM's own August 2022 survey found only 23% of members use the aranceles

arancel.publisher: Federación de Colegios de Arquitectos de la República Mexicana (CAN-FCARM), Aranceles Tomo I, Género habitacional
arancel.note: The worked example multiplies out without its stated FM of 1.10; the factor tables themselves are as printed.

feeAsPercent.note: No professional-body fee schedule published (NCSEA/ASCE do not publish). NAHB 2024 survey puts architecture+engineering combined at USD 6,480 per typical new house (1.5% of construction cost) - see costBySpec.US.nahb2024.

IE.note: Engineers Ireland publishes no fee scale.

MX.note: FCARM arancel lists 'Ingenierías' as one of four executive-project stages (FACP 0.040 applies when engineering is included); no separate engineering percentage published.

UK_IE.note: RICS and SCSI publish no survey fee scales. SCSI and RICS publish cost data used by quantity surveyors (see costBySpec).

medianPay.note: Employee wages; client hourly billing rates are not published by ASID or any government body.

other.note: No primary source for client billing rates in CA, MX, UK, IE.

value.caveats: National averages from 41 usable builder responses (fall 2024); no regional breakdown; not a spec-level survey.

nahb2024.publisher: National Association of Home Builders (Eric Lynch)

rlbQ2_2026_hardCostPerSqFtGFA.publisher: Rider Levett Bucknall, North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report Q2 2026
rlbQ2_2026_hardCostPerSqFtGFA.note: Low-high hard construction cost, USD per sq ft of gross floor area; low end approximates standard spec, high end high-end spec. Connecticut has no RLB city; Boston is the nearest listed. Column alignment was read from pdftotext layout output.

specTiers_standardMidHigh.note: No US primary source publishes a standard/mid/high-end per-sq-ft split for new homes. Use RLB low-high ranges and NAHB line items. RSMeans (paid) is the usual source.

secondStoryVsSingle.note: No US primary figure. BCIS-derived UK figures (below) show per-m2 cost rising slightly with storeys for one-off detached homes because roof and foundation are spread over more floor area differently; unconfirmed.

foundationMix2024.publisher: US Census Bureau Survey of Construction via NAHB

bathrooms.note: No primary per-bathroom new-build cost. For additions see materials.US.costVsValue2025 (bathroom addition midrange USD 60,645; upscale USD 111,255).

altus2025_perSqFtCAD.publisher: Altus Group, 2025 Canadian Cost Guide (primary PDF, rehosted by a third party)
altus2025_perSqFtCAD.note: Hard costs only. Standard vs high-end for a house maps to 'single family with unfinished basement' vs 'custom built single family'. Condo row alignment read from layout text.

altus2026_perSqFtCAD.publisher: Altus Group, 2026 Canadian Cost Guide (released 2026-04-23; data gated)
altus2026_perSqFtCAD.note: Figures from search summaries of the gated guide and a secondary reproduction (precedentdevelopments.ca), not read directly.

cmicCeico.publisher: Expansión reporting CMIC CEICO (Centro Nacional de Ingeniería de Costos) data
cmicCeico.note: Percent changes are from the Expansión article (read). Per-m2 figures came from search summaries of CMIC/IMIC catalog copies on Scribd and are unconfirmed. CMIC's own city report: https://www.cmic.org.mx/comisiones/Tematicas/costosyp/Informes_CEICO/INEGI/2025/04_Abril/CEICO_Informe_Abril_2025_Construccion_Residencial_por_Ciudad.pdf (not read).

fcarmBaseCost.unit: MXN per m2, Vivienda Social T11-CMIC, Nov 2022
fcarmBaseCost.note: See professionals.architects.MX; FGE factors 1.15 (tipo medio) and 1.30 (residencial) imply the profession's own relative cost of mid and high-end homes.

specTiersCDMX.note: BIMSA catalog (paid) is the primary source for interés social / media / residencial / residencial plus per m2; not accessible.

bcisOneOffHousing.note: BCIS (RICS) data are subscription-only. These show per-m2 cost rising modestly with storeys for one-off detached houses. Excludes land, VAT, fees and external works.

London.note: BCIS location factors (paid) put London above UK mean; no free primary figure.

scsiRebuild2025.publisher: Society of Chartered Surveyors Ireland, House Rebuilding Guide
scsiRebuild2025.note: Rebuild (insurance) cost for estate-type homes including demolition and site clearance; excludes kitchen, wardrobes, floor finishes. Values from search summary of the SCSI release.

scsiRealCostNewHousing2023.note: Most recent edition found; no 2025 edition located.

costVsValue2025_nationalJobCostUSD.publisher: Zonda / Journal of Light Construction, 38th annual Cost vs. Value Report
costVsValue2025_nationalJobCostUSD.note: Remodel/replacement job costs, not new-build increments. Read from a regional reprint PDF's National Averages column. A 2026 edition was not found as of 2026-09-30.

solarInstalledPrice.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Tracking the Sun / Distributed Solar and Storage 2025 Data Update
solarInstalledPrice.note: From search summary of LBNL release.

hvac.note: No primary installed-cost survey found; secondary ranges (furnace USD 4,000-10,000; heat pump USD 5,500-12,000) are unconfirmed. NAHB 2024 HVAC line item: USD 26,938 per new home (6.3%).

insulation.unit: USD per new home, NAHB 2024 (1.6% of construction)

flooring.note: No primary per-material split (hardwood vs LVP vs carpet vs tile).

CA.note: No primary material-by-material price survey found for ON or BC.

MX.note: BIMSA and CMIC catalogs (paid) hold material unit prices.

IE.note: SCSI rebuild guide excludes finishes; no public material split.

septic.note: Quoted via search summary; EPA page not read.

wellDrilling.note: NGWA publishes no public per-foot price; secondary sites cite USD 25-65 per foot and attribute it to NGWA surveys, unverified.

torontoDevelopmentCharges.note: Council removed indexing for 2025 and 2026. Secondary reports say a 60% cut for singles/semis and 2+ bedroom units applies to permits issued from June 2026 through 2029 under a provincial funding deal; not confirmed on toronto.ca.

vancouverDCL.note: Residential at or below 1.2 FSR after 20% temporary reduction effective 2025-12-10; secondary source, unconfirmed.

thamesWaterInfrastructure2025_26.publisher: Thames Water, Statement of Significant Change 2025-26
thamesWaterInfrastructure2025_26.note: Regulated utility charge (Ofwat rules); from search summary of the Thames Water document.

uisceEireannStandardConnection.unit: EUR per single domestic unit, up to 10 m of connection infrastructure

dublinCityDevelopmentContribution.unit: EUR per m2 residential, Section 48 scheme 2023-2026, indexed from 2025-04-01 (was 113.82)

MX.note: SACMEX water/drainage connection fees are set in the Código Fiscal de la CDMX; not extracted.

permitFee.value: USD 2.60 x building frontage in feet x number of stories, minimum USD 260 (as quoted)
permitFee.note: Formula from search summary of nyc.gov material. Local Law 128 of 2024 reportedly raised the general minimum fee to USD 130 effective 2025-12-21 (secondary).

newBuildingFee_1to3Family.value: USD 0.06 per sq ft of floor area, minimum USD 100 (LL 56 of 2016); minimum reportedly USD 130 after LL 128 of 2024
newBuildingFee_1to3Family.publisher: New York City Council, Int. 831-A (2015), amending Admin Code Table 28-112.2
newBuildingFee_1to3Family.note: Other new buildings: USD 0.26 per sq ft (fewer than 7 stories), USD 0.45 per sq ft (7+ stories or 100,000+ sq ft) per the same table.

process.value: Demolition pre-inspection by an LADBS inspector required before a demolition permit. For buildings over 45 years old, 30 days' notice: LADBS mails abutting owners/occupants, council district and neighborhood council; applicant posts an 11x17-inch placard within 5 ft of the front property line.
process.publisher: LA Department of Building and Safety (LAMC 91.106.4.5)

fee.note: Valuation-based; no flat residential demolition fee located. Demolition monitoring admin fee USD 45 (search summary).

US_CT.note: Municipal; CT adds a state education fee of USD 0.26 per USD 1,000 of construction value to every building permit (portal.ct.gov/das).

priorApprovalFee.unit: GBP, Part 11 Class B prior approval for demolition of buildings
priorApprovalFee.publisher: Town and Country Planning (Fees) (England) Regulations 2012 as amended 2025, indexed annually by CPI (cap 10%); schedule as published by a local planning authority
priorApprovalFee.note: From search summaries of council and Planning Portal fee schedules. Householder application fee from 2026-04-01: GBP 548.

planningRequirement.value: Demolition of a habitable house is not exempted development and needs planning permission (Planning and Development Regulations 2001 as amended). Partial demolition for an exempt extension is exempt; demolition of a terraced building or one abutting another owner's building is not exempt.

IE.levies: Landfill Levy change from 2024-09-01 and new Recovery Levy from 2025-01-01 raise demolition costs (SCSI 2025 release).

CA_ON.note: Toronto requires a demolition permit; fee not extracted.

MX_CDMX.note: Demolition requires a 'licencia de construcción especial' (demolición) from the Alcaldía; fees set in Código Fiscal CDMX (art. 185 covers manifestación fees). Amounts not extracted.

costPerUnitSmallMultiplex.note: No primary per-unit cost for duplex/triplex/fourplex in any market. Proxies: RLB multi-family per-sq-ft ranges (costBySpec.US.rlbQ2_2026_hardCostPerSqFtGFA) and Altus row/stacked townhouse ranges. Secondary sites quote USD 95,000-250,000 per fourplex unit, unconfirmed.

value.offeringPlanFilingFee: 0.4% of total offering, min USD 750 if offering <= USD 250,000, max USD 60,000 (was USD 30,000 before 2025-11-05)

US_NY.publisher: Nixon Peabody summarizing NY GBL 352-e amendments in the 2025-26 state budget
US_NY.note: Offering plan filed with the NY Attorney General Real Estate Finance Bureau under GBL 352-e and 13 NYCRR Part 20 (new construction) / Part 23 (conversion).

US_CA.publisher: California Department of Real Estate, RE 605 (Rev. 7/26)
US_CA.note: Subdivision public report fees. Tentative/final map and conversion rules are local.

value.cao_assessment: CAD 1 per voting unit per month

CA_ON.publisher: Government of Ontario, Land Registration bulletin
CA_ON.note: CAO fee from condoauthorityontario.ca via search summary (unconfirmed). Tarion new-home warranty enrolment also applies (fee not extracted).

CA_BC.note: Strata plan under the Strata Property Act; fees not extracted.

UK.value: Leasehold is the default for flats. Commonhold White Paper published 2025-03-03; draft Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill published 2026-01-27 proposing to end new leasehold flats in England and Wales; consultation closed 2026-04-24. Not yet law as of 2026-09-30.

MX_CDMX.value: Régimen de propiedad en condominio is constituted by public deed before a notary, registered with the Registro Público and with PROSOC; requires an internal regulation. Governed by the Ley de Propiedad en Condominio de Inmuebles para la CDMX; fiscal basis Código Fiscal CDMX art. 430 (as cited).
MX_CDMX.publisher: Procuraduría Social de la Ciudad de México

IE.note: Multi-Unit Developments Act 2011 governs owners' management companies; no filing fee located.

US_buildTimes2025.publisher: NAHB Eye on Housing, analysis of US Census Bureau Survey of Construction
US_buildTimes2025.note: Contractor-built (11.7) is the relevant path for a character hiring a builder; owner-built (14.3) for self-managed. New England covers CT.

mckinsey.value: Large projects typically take 20% longer than scheduled and run up to 80% over budget

kpmg.value: Only 25% of large projects finished within 10% of original deadlines over the prior three years (2015 survey)

dodgeMaterialDelays.value: 57% of contractors had at least one project delayed by material lead times in the prior year (2024 survey, as quoted)

changeOrders.note: No primary residential change-order statistic found. Commonly repeated '10-15% of contract value on major projects' and 'CII: 5-10% contract growth' trace to academic/CII work on large industrial projects, not homes; unconfirmed.

UK_HBF_2024.publisher: Home Builders Federation, National New Home Customer Satisfaction Survey (completions Oct 2022-Sep 2023)
UK_HBF_2024.note: The four band shares were extracted from a pie chart whose label-to-slice mapping could not be read reliably; the values are confirmed, their band assignment is not. 2026 release (2026-03-24): 93% would recommend, 90% satisfied with quality, 88% with after-sales, 20% reported fewer snags than expected.

US_general.value: AIA A101 (owner-contractor, stipulated sum) with A201 General Conditions: monthly applications for payment certified by the architect; retainage percentage left blank for the parties. Market practice 5-10%.

value.appliesTo: private construction contracts of USD 150,000 or more entered on/after 2023-11-17
value.releaseDeadline: within 30 days after final approval of the work

US_NY.publisher: Holland & Knight on NY GBL 756-a/756-c (S3539, signed 2023-11-17)

value.appliesTo: private works contracts entered on/after 2026-01-01 (Civil Code 8811, SB 61)
value.exception: up to 10% from a subcontractor who fails to furnish required bonds

US_CT.note: CT Prompt Payment Act (CGS 42-158i et seq.) caps private retainage at 7.5% (commonly cited); not verified in this pass.

value.annualHoldbackRelease: mandatory from 2026 amendments; accrued holdback paid 60-74 days after notice of annual release

CA_ON.publisher: DLA Piper on Ontario Construction Act

value.pendingChange: Construction Prompt Payment Act will cut holdback period to 46 days on coming into force

CA_BC.note: 10% holdback cannot be reduced by contract.

value.jctMinorWorks: 5% retention on interim certificates, halved to 2.5% at practical completion, balance released after the rectification period (default 3 months in MW 2011; commonly 6-12 months)
value.policy: Government announced 2026-03-24 its intention to ban cash retentions (consultation closed 2025-10-23; 12-24 month transition expected); not yet law
value.newBuildPurchaseDeposit: 10% at exchange; NHBC Buildmark protects deposit up to GBP 100,000 or 10% of price

value.cca2013: Payment claim dates every 30 days from commencement; response within 21 days
value.exemptions: contracts <= EUR 10,000, or a dwelling <= 200 m2 where a party occupies or intends to occupy it
value.retentionPractice: RIAI forms provide for retention; Liaison Committee Code of Practice: 7.5% under EUR 500,000, 5% for EUR 500,000-1,000,000; half released at practical completion, half after defects liability period

IE.publisher: Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment; Liaison Committee (https://liaisoncommittee.ie/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Code-Of-Practice-2018.pdf)
IE.note: The owner-occupier house exemption means most one-off home builds fall outside the CCA 2013.

MX.value: Private contracts are free-form. Public works (LOPSRM) require guarantees for advances and performance within 15 days of award (art. 48) and a hidden-defects guarantee released 12 months after physical handover (art. 66). The specific percentages (advance commonly up to 30%, performance 10%) are set by each agency and were not verified.

US_NYC.steps: All sign-offs, fees paid, violations resolved, other-agency approvals; CO worksheet for final CO or TCO. Records management fee on new-building applications: USD 45 for 1-3 family, USD 165 other (1 RCNY 101-03, confirmed).

US_LA.note: C of O issued by LADBS after final inspection passes on new construction.

US_CT.value: No building may be occupied until the local building official issues a certificate of occupancy certifying substantial compliance with the State Building Code; fee set by each town.

CA_ON.value: Occupancy permit under OBC Division C 1.3.3; for unfinished buildings Toronto issues an 'Authority to Occupy' permit, applied for at least 10 business days before occupancy, once structure, walls, fire separations, exits, water/drainage, lighting, heating and fire alarm are complete.

CA_BC.note: Vancouver issues occupancy permits after final inspection; fee not extracted.

UK_England.value: Completion certificate issued by local authority building control or a registered building control approver; the charge is included in plan + inspection fees set by each authority (example: GBP 200 plan + GBP 1,300 inspection incl. VAT for one new dwelling at one authority, 2025).
UK_England.publisher: Local authority charging schedules (Building (Local Authority Charges) Regulations 2010)
UK_England.note: London boroughs set their own (e.g. Lambeth schedule https://www.lambeth.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2024-04/Building_Control_Guide_to_Fees_2024_2025_0.pdf); not extracted.

value.noticeWindow: not more than 28 and not less than 14 days before works start
value.completion: Certificate of Compliance on Completion (BCAR) must be lodged and entered on the statutory register before the building is occupied

IE.publisher: Irish Point of Single Contact / Building Control Management System

MX_CDMX.value: Owner files the Aviso de Terminación de Obra with the Alcaldía (or SEDUVI) within 15 business days of completion; the authority checks the work against the Reglamento de Construcciones and issues the Autorización de Uso y Ocupación. Partial notices allowed for independently operating parts. Manifestación tipo B covers non-residential/mixed up to 5,000 m2 or up to 10,000 m2 residential; fees under Código Fiscal CDMX art. 185.
MX_CDMX.publisher: Gobierno de la Ciudad de México

uncertain: No free primary source splits new-home cost by specification tier (standard/mid/high) in the US, UK or Mexico; RSMeans, BCIS and BIMSA are paywalled. RLB low/high and Altus standard vs custom are the best primary proxies.
Second-story vs single-story, basement per sq ft, attached garage (except SCSI Ireland) and per-bathroom new-build increments have no primary figures in any market.
Altus 2026 figures are from summaries of a gated guide; the 2025 guide was read directly.
HBF 2024 problem-count bands: values read, band mapping not.
NYC demolition fee formula and LL 128 of 2024 minimum-fee change not read from the statute text.
UK retention ban announced 2026-03-24 but not enacted; UK commonhold reform is a draft bill.
Toronto 2026 development-charge 60% reduction reported by secondary sources only.
Mexico CMIC per-m2 figures by housing class came from catalog copies and summaries, not CMIC directly.
Change-order percentages for residential work have no primary statistic; large-project figures (McKinsey, KPMG) should not be applied to single homes without that caveat.
Zonda Cost vs Value 2026 edition not found as of 2026-09-30; 2025 (released 2025-09-18) is the latest used.
Several search-engine summaries contained anachronistic or unverifiable political details (e.g. a named UK prime minister); these were excluded.
